# **Architectural Analysis of OOXML Package Handling, Determinism, and Supply-Chain Security for jubarte-redlines**

## **Executive Summary and Ecosystem Landscape**

Engineering a high-assurance Office Open XML (OOXML) redlining engine—jubarte-redlines—requires reconciling two fundamentally opposing architectural forces. On one hand, a .docx file is an Open Packaging Conventions (OPC, ECMA-376 Part 2 / ISO/IEC 29500-2) ZIP archive containing interrelated XML parts (word/document.xml, word/comments.xml, word/footnotes.xml, word/styles.xml, \_rels/.rels, \[Content\_Types\].xml) and binary media payloads1. Injecting tracked changes (w:ins, w:del, w:rPrChange, w:pPrChange) and reviewer comments demands fine-grained manipulation of character runs, revision identifiers, and whitespace boundaries (xml:space="preserve")3. On the other hand, enterprise legal, regulatory, and agentic workflows require strict byte-level preservation of unmodeled document structures, deterministic output digests for cryptographic attestation, bounded memory execution against adversarial inputs, and an auditable dependency graph free of yanked or vulnerable archive parsers6.  
A cross-sectional study of fourteen reference implementations across the Rust and Python document-processing ecosystems—docx2typed-review, office\_oxide, text-document, mt-docx, docx2typed, docmux-writer-docx, docmux-reader-docx, stella-docx-kernel 0.38.0, rightkit-docs, quilldown 1.5.0, docling-core, rwml 0.1.5, imprimatur 0.2.0, and docling 2.35.0—reveals that document libraries bifurcate into four distinct architectural archetypes. Only two of these archetypes preserve the structural invariants required for production redlining, while the broader Rust ecosystem is simultaneously navigating a severe supply-chain disruption triggered by the October 2026 security yanks of all pre-9.0.2 versions of the foundational zip crate11.

## **The October 2026 Rust ZIP Supply-Chain Crisis and I/O Mechanics**

The most urgent operational constraint for jubarte-redlines concerns the underlying ZIP archive layer in Rust. In October 2026, the maintainers of the zip crate (github.com/zip-rs/zip2) executed an ecosystem-wide security intervention by yanking all versions prior to the 9.0.x release series, alongside early 9.0.x releases up to 9.0.1, leaving zip v9.0.2 as the active patched release11. While Cargo permits projects with pre-existing Cargo.lock files to continue fetching yanked crate archives from the registry so existing builds do not immediately break, any fresh dependency resolution (cargo add, cargo update), binary installation (cargo install), or automated supply-chain check (cargo audit, cargo deny check advisories) flags yanked versions such as zip 2.2.3, zip 4.0, or zip 8.6.0 as fatal policy violations11. A temporary reprieve window extending until October 30, 2026, was noted by maintainers to allow downstream maintainers to backport fixes or upgrade dependency trees before permanent yanks lock out legacy versions11.  
This mass yank originated from high-severity extraction and resource-exhaustion vulnerabilities disclosed against zip-rs/zip2 (Issue \#1075)11. The primary vulnerability, GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp (tracked also as AIKIDO-2026-476773 and rated High severity across versions up to 9.0.1), resides in ZipStreamReader::extract() (src/read/stream.rs:89-109), where Unix permissions (std::fs::set\_permissions) are applied during a post-extraction central directory metadata pass (visit\_additional\_metadata()) using outpath \= base.join(metadata.enclosed\_name()?) without re-validating whether outpath resolves through an extracted symlink pointing outside the destination root13. During the preceding file-extraction pass (src/read/stream.rs:63-86), ZipFile::safe\_prepare\_path (src/read.rs:857-968) checked existing filesystem symlink path components via read\_link, but broke out of its validation loop on NotFound for the final component when creating a new symlink via make\_symlink(\&outpath, \&target, ...), leaving the attacker-controlled target unchecked until the subsequent set\_permissions sink followed it outside the sandbox13. Simultaneously, GHSA-q7v9-x93c-xqv3 exposed unbounded symlink-target handling capable of aborting execution or exhausting process memory during extraction62, while RUSTSEC-2026-0177 highlighted zip-bomb denial-of-service vectors in downstream parsers that fail to bound decompression streams36.  
![][image4]

### **Direct Consumers of Legacy zip 2.x (docx2typed, docmux, rwml)**

Despite active development in late 2026, several of the evaluated Rust packages remain pinned to the zip 2.x major series and are therefore directly impacted by the registry yanks. Within the docx2typed workspace (v0.1.0-rc1 / v0.2.0), docx2typed-core and the root crate's dev-dependencies specify zip 2.0+deflate, while docx2typed-review delegates direct archive persistence to docx2typed-store15. Similarly, docmux-reader-docx 0.6.2 and docmux-writer-docx 0.6.2 (published October 15, 2026\) declare zip ^2 alongside quick-xml ^0.37 and thiserror ^235. In rwml 0.1.5 (and its 0.1.4 documentation baseline), legacy Word 97–2003 .doc files are parsed through cfb ^0.10, while modern .docx support is gated behind the docx Cargo feature, which pulls in zip ^2.2 and quick-xml ^0.41 as optional dependencies51. If jubarte-redlines were to depend directly on docmux-reader-docx, docx2typed-core, or rwml with features \= \["docx"\], Cargo's dependency resolver would either fail to resolve yanked zip ^2 versions in a clean environment or introduce a duplicate, vulnerable zip dependency into the workspace graph11.

### **Early zip 9.0 Adopters (mt-docx) and Bounded Scanners (stella-docx-kernel)**

In contrast, the mt-docx 0.1.2 and mt-batch 0.1.2 workspace (published October 14, 2026\) has already migrated its ZIP dependency to zip ^9.034. Adopting zip 9.0.2 resolves the security yanks, though it imposes a Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) of 1.88.0 and Rust 2024 edition semantics12. Furthermore, because zip 9.0.2 enables aes-crypto, bzip2, deflate, deflate64, lzma, ppmd, time, xz, and zstd by default12, an OOXML engine using zip 9.0.2 must explicitly configure default-features \= false, features \= \["deflate"\] (or "deflate-flate2") in Cargo.toml to avoid compiling seven unnecessary compression and encryption backends that standard ECMA-376 .docx packages never utilize12.  
An even stricter architectural separation is demonstrated by stella-docx-kernel 0.38.0 (and its 0.28.0 documented lineage). Designed to project bounded DOCX packages into a versioned, host-neutral document representation across native Rust and wasm32 targets (features \= \["wasm"\]), stella-docx-kernel isolates external zip crate usage (zip ^8.3.0) strictly to dev-dependencies for test fixture generation while enforcing bounded ZIP and XML scanning internally10. Similarly, enterprise vertical kits such as rightkit-docs and attestation layers such as imprimatur 0.2.0 operate over pre-validated package buffers and virtualized part maps rather than exposing raw filesystem extraction routines to downstream callers18.

### **Custom OPC Layers, Delegated Writers, and Zero-Dependency rawzip**

At the high-performance end of the spectrum, office\_oxide (v0.1.13–0.1.15, MSRV 1.88.0) implements a dedicated Open Packaging Conventions module (core::opc in opc.rs) containing OpcReader and OpcWriter alongside a custom Compound File Binary (CFB) reader for legacy .doc, .xls, and .ppt formats25. Rather than treating a .docx as an arbitrary filesystem directory tree, OpcReader treats the archive as an indexed map of OPC parts and relationship tables, achieving a ![][image5] mean parse time across its DOCX benchmark corpus26.  
Conversely, text-document (v1.12.5) and quilldown (v1.5.0) do not implement general-purpose OPC read-modify-write engines. In text-document-io, export\_docx\_uc.rs delegates .docx archive construction to docx-rs (v0.4.22), leans on epub-builder ^0.8.3 for EPUBs, and maintains a separate odt\_render.rs module solely for OpenDocument (ODT) ZIP packaging30. quilldown 1.5.0 (quilldown-cli) parses GitHub-Flavored Markdown via comrak and synthesizes a fresh .docx ZIP archive in a single forward pass40. Finally, in the Python ecosystem, docling 2.35.0 delegates .docx reading to python-docx 1.2.0 (which wraps Python's standard library zipfile.ZipFile and lxml), converting the content into the DoclingDocument schema defined by docling-core (v2.101.1, or v2.13.0 in the docling.rs Rust port)47.  
For jubarte-redlines, the optimal Rust ZIP foundation is either rawzip v0.5.2 (MIT, MSRV 1.85.0, 6.8K SLoC, zero dependencies, zero unsafe, zero-allocation central directory lending iterator via ZipArchive::from\_slice or ZipArchive::from\_file, paired with flate2) or zip v9.0.2 configured with default-features \= false, features \= \["deflate"\]9. rawzip is particularly compelling for an in-memory or memory-mapped redlining kernel because it avoids materializing the central directory with heap allocations—delivering ![][image6] to ![][image7] lower structural overhead than traditional ZIP libraries—and provides explicit ZipArchiveWriter and verifying\_reader hooks where the caller controls the exact flate2 encoder and CRC32 verifier9.

## **Byte Determinism, Unmodeled Part Preservation, and Coordinate-Stable Redlining**

A redlining engine stands or falls on its preservation contract. When a legal or enterprise user submits a complex contract .docx containing custom styles, embedded Excel charts (xl/embeddings/oleObject1.bin), DrawingML diagrams, custom XML data bindings, and existing tracked changes, the output .docx must retain every unmodeled byte intact while deterministically injecting the new redline markup2.  
![][image8]

### **The Failure Mode of Full AST Re-Serialization**

Six of the studied packages—text-document, docmux-reader-docx, docmux-writer-docx, quilldown 1.5.0, docling-core, and docling 2.35.0 (as well as rwml 0.1.5's write\_docx synthesis path)—operate via abstract syntax tree (AST) or intermediate representation (IR) projection29. In docmux-reader-docx 0.6.2 and docmux-writer-docx 0.6.2, the input .docx binary is parsed into a docmux-ast Document struct and subsequently re-serialized from scratch when writing35. Similarly, in text-document, import and export routines in text-document-io map paragraphs and runs into a ropey::Rope character buffer with byte-ranged FormatRun and ImageAnchor structs, then invoke docx-rs (Docx::collect\_footnotes(), etc.) to pack a newly generated .docx archive on export29. In docling 2.35.0 and docling-core, DocumentConverter normalizes .docx inputs (via python-docx 1.2.0) into DoclingDocument trees designed for RAG pipelines, visual language models (GraniteDocling), Markdown, DocTags, and lossless JSON export46.  
While AST projection is well suited for cross-format conversion, GPU quad typesetting (text-typeset), or AI ingestion, full AST re-serialization is destructive for jubarte-redlines8. As documented in comparative OOXML audits (such as rdocx's capability matrix and ooxmlsdk's 5,477-file round-trip test suite), libraries like docx-rs parse only into the subset model used by their writer and drop unmodeled producer XML, whereas python-docx leaves unmanipulated parts alone on load and save but provides no byte-exact guarantee on modified XML streams8.

### **Pass-Through OPC Part Cloning (office\_oxide and docx2typed-store)**

To prevent package degradation during editing, office\_oxide separates read-only extraction (Document) from structure-preserving mutation (EditableDocument)27. When EditableDocument::open("template.docx") executes replace\_text and save("out.docx"), office\_oxide's OpcWriter preserves every unmodified OPC part—images, embedded charts, numbering definitions, themes, and .rels relationships—byte-for-byte from the source OpcReader archive, re-serializing only the mutated XML part26.  
The docx2typed workspace (github.com/LLLin000/docx2typed) elevates this preservation model into a transactional, verifiable state machine tailored for agentic and human-in-the-loop review15. Within this architecture, docx2typed-store (v0.1.0-rc1) implements workdir commit, byte-copy build publish, and canonical evidence and manifest publication (Issue \#55), paired with an independent read-only verifier (docx2typed-core) that validates canonical JSON and revision diagnostics (docx2typed-protocol v0.2.0) before any package bytes are finalized15. Rather than allowing a browser UI or external script to mutate the .docx archive behind the agent's back, docx2typed-review (v0.1.0-rc1, implementing Issue \#60) introduces an external-write guard in its collab module and an atomic review frame (docx2typed-review-frame-1) in its frame module17. Under this contract, a single store pin yields one consistent read model combining the Core document projection, the file-backed review event queue (.review/inbox), the session state machine (SNAPSHOT\_SCHEMA, PATCH\_SCHEMA), and the generation-bound review trail (.review/history.jsonl)23. The browser console renders tracked changes across three synchronized lenses—修订 (tracked redlines), 最终 (final accepted view), and 原文 (original baseline)—while queuing reviewer decisions into .review/inbox so that settlement into the .docx occurs strictly through the guarded Rust store transaction17.

### **Reverse-Order Byte-Offset Splicing (mt-docx)**

Even when unmodified ZIP entries are cloned verbatim, re-serializing an entire word/document.xml DOM through an XML writer (quick-xml or lxml) can alter attribute ordering, namespace prefixes, self-closing tag syntax (\<w:p/\> versus \<w:p\>\</w:p\>), and whitespace normalization across untouched paragraphs. mt-docx 0.1.2 (and its batch orchestrator mt-batch 0.1.2) solves this inside word/document.xml via reverse document-order byte splicing34. During its dry-run planning phase (plan), mt-docx scans word/document.xml—optionally restricted to a caller-supplied byte range via Options::scope when a host Word add-in passes a user selection—and records the exact byte coordinates of every target item (PlanItem) without mutating the document34.  
When executing in replacement mode (Mode::Replace), mt-docx rewrites word/document.xml in reverse document order, progressing from the highest byte offset at the end of the document back toward the beginning34. Because a byte splice over range ![][image9] only shifts byte offsets at indices strictly greater than ![][image10], the byte coordinates ![][image11] of all pending items earlier in the document (![][image12]) are never invalidated by an edit34. If an individual item conversion fails during the pass, mt-docx records a structured failure tuple (序号, 位置, 原因)—item sequence number, byte position, and failure cause—and continues the run; if the progress callback returns false, execution aborts cleanly while preserving all edits already spliced34. Furthermore, as demonstrated in Pandoc's DOCX reader and writer fixes (\#11904), surgical redline splicers must keep leading and trailing spaces at the edges of tracked changes inside the \<w:ins\> or \<w:del\> span with explicit whitespace preservation so Word does not collapse word boundaries when changes are reviewed5.

### **Container-Level Byte Determinism (imprimatur 0.2.0 and Cryptographic Attestation)**

For jubarte-redlines to achieve full container-level byte determinism—where applying identical redline patches to the same input .docx across Linux, macOS, Windows, or wasm32 produces an identical SHA-256 archive digest suitable for imprimatur 0.2.0 publication sign-off, zipsign signature verification (self\_update / zipsign-api), or c2pa-text JUMBF manifest embedding54—surgical XML splicing must be paired with canonical ZIP container assembly. By default, ZIP writers stamp entries with the host system clock via time or chrono features and iterate over hash maps with randomized per-process SipHash seeds12. A deterministic redlining writer must preserve original central directory ordering via an IndexMap (appending newly created parts such as word/comments.xml in deterministic lexicographical order), pin last\_modified\_time on modified headers to a fixed MS-DOS epoch constant (or preserve original header timestamps verbatim), enforce Unicode NFC filename normalization with UTF-8 bit flags and zero OS-specific extra fields (nt-time), and pin a deterministic flate2 compression level rather than relying on zip 9.0.2's unspecified default deflate backend12.

## **Resource Safety Caps, Decompression Ceilings, and DoS Mitigation**

Because .docx files are routinely ingested from untrusted external counterparties, a redlining engine is a prime target for Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks via decompression amplification (ZIP bombs such as RUSTSEC-2026-0177), overlapping ZIP local file headers, quadratic XML expansion, or deeply nested WordprocessingML tables9.

### **Bounded Ingress Scanning (stella-docx-kernel 0.38.0 and rawzip)**

stella-docx-kernel 0.38.0 establishes the structural benchmark among the studied Rust crates by treating all input archives as untrusted and enforcing strict ZIP and XML resource limits directly at the package projection and WordprocessingML scanner boundary10. Rather than trusting the central directory's declared uncompressed\_size field—which an adversary can spoof as a small integer while streaming gigabytes of decompressed bytes through DEFLATE9—a bounded kernel enforces hard streaming ceilings. As rawzip's security architecture explicitly notes, while a low-level archive reader provides memory safety, structural validation of the End of Central Directory (EOCD), central directory, and local file headers, and opt-in CRC32/size verification (verifying\_reader), the consuming application must enforce maximum compression ratios, maximum uncompressed file sizes (via std::io::Read::take), checks against overlapping local file header data ranges, limits on central directory entry counts, and defenses against recursive ZIP quines9. Pairing rawzip's zero-allocation central directory iterator with stella-docx-kernel's bounded XML depth and token budgets ensures that malformed or weaponized .docx archives are rejected in constant memory before DOM or AST allocation begins9.

### **Application-Layer Output and State Budgets (office\_oxide, quilldown, rwml, text-document)**

Beyond the archive parser, the studied packages implement explicit resource ceilings at the semantic document layer. To guarantee zero panics and zero timeouts across its 6,062-document benchmark corpus, office\_oxide enforces a default per-document rendered text budget of ![][image1] characters (![][image13] characters)25. When a document exceeds this budget, the renderer halts cleanly, appends a visible \[output truncated: …\] notice, and sets Metadata::text\_truncated \= true; processes that legitimately handle massive workbooks can raise the ceiling once at startup via office\_oxide::limits::set\_max\_text\_chars(1 \<\< 30\)25. Similarly, quilldown 1.5.0 bounds its serialized share-link payloads by issuing a user warning above ![][image2] characters, enforcing a hard refusal ceiling at ![][image3] characters, and stripping pasted binary images from link state44.  
In rwml 0.1.5, resource and parser safety begins with immediate header refusal: if the File Information Block (FIB) indicates encryption or obfuscation (fEncrypted), rwml refuses extraction with Error::Encrypted { obfuscated: bool } (distinguishing \[MS-DOC\] 2.2.6.1 XOR obfuscation from RC4/CryptoAPI encryption) rather than emitting scrambled bytes or looping over corrupt piece tables (Error::PieceTable), and rejects pre-Word-97 layouts (nFib \< 0x00C1) with Error::UnsupportedVersion(u16)52. Meanwhile, text-document bounds interactive memory growth through an optional undo stack depth cap (set\_undo\_limit) alongside an untracked write stack for programmatic operations that must not accumulate snapshot history29, and mt-docx / mt-batch clamps rasterized formula dimensions and resolution using MIN\_DPI, DEFAULT\_DPI, MIN\_SIZE, and DEFAULT\_SIZE (![][image14]) constants34.

## **Path Traversal, Symlink Containment, and OPC URI Normalization**

Path traversal in .docx processing spans two distinct threat surfaces: filesystem extraction (when a library unpacks archive entries or writes review queues to disk) and virtual OPC URI resolution (when an in-memory parser resolves \[Content\_Types\].xml and \_rels/\*.rels relationship targets)9.

### **Filesystem Extraction Vulnerabilities and Workdir Hardening**

The October 2026 disclosure of GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp in zip \<= 9.0.1 illustrates why invoking filesystem extraction helpers such as ZipStreamReader::extract() on untrusted .docx containers creates severe exposure13. Even though metadata.enclosed\_name() filtered basic .. path traversal segments, extracting a symlink entry followed by a central directory Unix permission pass (visit\_additional\_metadata) caused std::fs::set\_permissions to follow the symlink outside the destination directory, mutating permissions on external host files or aborting extraction13.  
Across the studied packages, office\_oxide, stella-docx-kernel 0.38.0, rwml 0.1.5, docmux-reader-docx 0.6.2, and text-document eliminate filesystem extraction vulnerabilities entirely by operating strictly in memory over byte slices (&\[u8\]) or Read \+ Seek streams, never materializing ZIP entries or symlinks onto the host disk10. Where disk persistence is architecturally required for multi-step collaboration, docx2typed and docx2typed-review 0.1.0-rc1 harden their working directory (workdir) and file-backed queue (.review/inbox and .review/history.jsonl) using the Issue \#31 transport-security contract (security module), which enforces capability verification, Host allowlists, Origin gates, request throttling, HTTP security headers, and an external-write guard (collab module) that detects and rejects unauthorized out-of-band file modifications23. Similarly, when mt-docx / mt-batch writes exported formula files in Mode::Export, it validates the target directory via ensure\_export\_dir and synthesizes strictly sequential internal filenames (eq001.tex, eq001.mml, eq001.omml, eq001.png) rather than interpolating untrusted paths from the .docx archive34.

### **In-Memory OPC URI Normalization and Relationship Containment**

Even in a zero-disk, in-memory redlining engine, logical path traversal and semantic parser differentials (as documented in the USENIX Security '25 research *"My ZIP isn't your ZIP: Identifying and Exploiting Semantic Gaps Between ZIP Parsers"* cited by rawzip) can corrupt internal part lookup tables69. Different OOXML producers emit entry names with leading slashes (/word/document.xml), Windows backslashes (word\\document.xml), relative dot segments (word/./\_rels/../document.xml), or duplicate central directory entries with identical normalized names to shadow legitimate parts9. jubarte-redlines should adopt rawzip 0.5.2's explicit path normalization (entry.file\_path().try\_normalize()?) to canonicalize internal paths, reject any entry containing .., null bytes, or drive prefixes, and reject archives containing duplicate normalized entry names9. Simultaneously, when parsing \_rels/\*.rels and document links, jubarte-redlines must block any external dereferencing (TargetMode="External", file:///, UNC paths, or remote template fetching bugs such as the template-fetching vulnerability patched in Pandoc 3.8) so that relationship resolution is hermetically confined to the in-memory OPC part table5.

## **Licensing, Dependency Graphs, and CI Policy Enforcement**

A comprehensive dependency and licensing audit across the fourteen studied packages highlights critical version divergences in XML parsers (quick-xml ^0.37 versus ^0.41), ZIP backends (zip ^2 / ^8.3 / ^9.0 versus rawzip ^0.5.2), and Rust Minimum Supported Rust Versions (1.75 to 1.88+)12.

All evaluated core libraries utilize permissive open-source licenses—MIT (quilldown, rwml, docling, docling-core, zip, rawzip, docx-rs), Apache-2.0 (stella-docx-kernel), or dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 (office\_oxide, ooxmlsdk)—enabling unrestricted commercial and enterprise integration12. office\_oxide explicitly highlights its dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 licensing to contrast with GPL-2.0 legacy extractors such as xls2csv and AGPL document toolkits25. When assembling the dependency graph for jubarte-redlines, engineers must avoid lookalike crates in the broader ecosystem that carry copyleft obligations, such as textframe v0.4.1 (GPL-3.0-only) or async-opcua (MPL-2.0)81.  
To harden jubarte-redlines against supply-chain shocks—including both the October 2026 zip security yanks and build-time payload attacks such as the August 20, 2026 compromise of the arrayref crate (RUSTSEC advisory DB Issue \#3161, which executed a malicious build script before being removed 86 minutes after publication)—the repository should adopt the CI governance model exemplified by ryll and pqc-sig6. Specifically, CI must execute both cargo-deny (deny.toml) and cargo-audit (.cargo/audit.toml) on every pull request and weekly schedule, keeping any temporary advisory or yanked-crate ignore entries strictly synchronized with inline rationale comments across both files (or declared transparently in SECURITY.md)6. Furthermore, deny.toml should set multiple-versions \= "deny" on core parsers (rawzip, zip, flate2, quick-xml), restrict allow-build-scripts to prevent unauthorized build.rs execution in a pure-Rust (no C compiler) build environment, and validate clean-room cargo package artifacts alongside a standalone wasm32-unknown-unknown downstream consumer fixture7.

## **Architectural Synthesis and Recommendations for jubarte-redlines**

Synthesizing the empirical mechanics of all fourteen packages yields a cohesive, high-assurance blueprint for jubarte-redlines. At the archive I/O layer, jubarte-redlines should adopt rawzip v0.5.2 (MIT, MSRV 1.85.0, zero dependencies, zero unsafe) paired with flate2 and quick-xml ^0.419. Using rawzip::ZipArchive::from\_slice provides zero-allocation central directory traversal, while local\_entry.verifying\_reader(decompressor) guarantees CRC32 and uncompressed size validation on every read9. If the zip crate is included anywhere in the workspace (such as in dev-dependencies for cross-validation fixtures, mirroring stella-docx-kernel), it must be pinned to zip \= { version \= "9.0.2", default-features \= false, features \= \["deflate"\] } to eliminate all pre-9.0.2 security yanks (GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp, GHSA-q7v9-x93c-xqv3) and strip seven unneeded compression backends11.  
At the document mutation and preservation layer, jubarte-redlines should reject full AST re-serialization (docmux-reader-docx, docmux-writer-docx, text-document-io, quilldown) in favor of a hybrid architecture that combines office\_oxide's pass-through OPC part cloning (OpcReader/OpcWriter) and docx2typed-store's byte-copy publish with mt-docx's reverse document-order byte splicing15. All incoming ZIP entries should be indexed in an order-preserving IndexMap and copied verbatim to the output writer unless explicitly targeted for redlining13. Within word/document.xml, planned \<w:ins\>, \<w:del\>, and comment range markers should be spliced in reverse byte-offset order so earlier document coordinates remain invariant, boundary whitespace is preserved inside revision runs (\#11904), untouched XML regions remain byte-identical, and fixed MS-DOS timestamps plus NFC path normalization guarantee deterministic SHA-256 output digests for imprimatur 0.2.0 attestation5.  
Finally, to ensure resilience against adversarial inputs and multi-user race conditions, jubarte-redlines should enforce stella-docx-kernel 0.38.0's bounded ingress gates—capping total archive bytes, central directory entry counts, compression ratios, non-overlapping local header ranges, per-part Read::take decompression ceilings, and quick-xml nesting depth—combined with office\_oxide's configurable ![][image1] character budget and rwml 0.1.5's immediate refusal of encrypted containers9. All core redlining operations should execute strictly in memory with rawzip's try\_normalize() path validation and zero external .rels dereferencing, while interactive browser or agent review lanes should adopt docx2typed-review 0.1.0-rc1's atomic review frame (docx2typed-review-frame-1), capability-gated .review/inbox queue, .review/history.jsonl audit trail, and external-write guard, keeping optional Python or VLM verification harnesses (python-oracle, docling-core) disabled by default so the workspace remains fast, deterministic, and hermetically testable9.
